series.title: Building the Batcave
series.description: A multi-agent AI system that started on Telegram and grew into a nutrition app on my phone and wrist: the architecture, the app, the platform underneath it, memory, evals, and the agent at the center.
series.source_brief: BUILD_IN_PUBLIC.md in the project-batcave repo holds the editorial briefs (hooks, engineering moments, concrete numbers). Read it for grounding before writing any part, and verify claims against the code: the briefs were written 2026-10-22 and the repo moves daily.

parts.brief: Intro / architecture post for the whole system. The system is a multi-agent AI assistant reachable over Telegram (text, voice, photos). It started Open-Claw-inspired on a GCP Always Free e2-micro running PM2 + Telegram long-polling, which worked until the Claude Agent SDK started spawning child Node processes and the 1 GB box got OOM-killed in a restart loop. The arc to today, told as the real evolution (do NOT describe the dead VM/PM2 stack as current): hand-rolled multi-agent with shared-context handoffs -> Agent SDK query() with isolated subagent contexts + Supabase Postgres for durable state (sessions resume by session_id, survive restarts) -> Cloud Run + webhook + Cloud Tasks, because you cannot run long-polling on a scale-to-zero container and Telegram allows exactly one getUpdates consumer per bot token. The decoupling insight is the spine: an agentic turn takes 10-30s (Whisper -> Haiku router -> Claude Sonnet loop -> ElevenLabs), longer than Telegram's webhook retry window, so the ingest service acks in <100ms, enqueues a Cloud Task, and the worker gets 300s. Idempotency comes free from Cloud Tasks named tasks (update-<update_id> drops Telegram redeliveries). Cost arithmetic: the free e2-micro kept dying, an always-on Cloud Run worker pool was ~$45/mo, webhook + scale-to-zero is ~$0-5/mo; the cost was idle time, not RAM. Introduce the cast the next three posts profile: a Haiku router classifies each message (gordon/ras/alfred/unclear) for ~$0.0003 before anyone sees it; Alfred is the top-level conversational agent; Gordon and Ra's are subagents in isolated contexts. The MCP server is IN-PROCESS via createSdkMcpServer (not a separate external service) and talks to Supabase. Mention the 5-suite eval framework briefly (routing gates PRs, the rest run nightly) but save the depth for later. 'Production-grade' is a banned phrase: show what production actually cost (the OOM kill, the trailing newline in Secret Manager that left the webhook unregistered, the wrong ogg_opus format name that silently killed voice replies). Include one Mermaid diagram of the full request path (Telegram -> ingest -> Cloud Tasks -> worker -> orchestrator -> router/agents -> MCP -> Supabase). This is Part 1 so there is no previous part to link.

The personal hook post. An impromptu trip to Punta Cana got booked, and a number on the scale was not Dark Knight worthy. Do NOT state the number or any weight figure. Context: lots of CrossFit and kitesurfing, but no food tracking, so the training was not showing up. That pushed Gordon from a Telegram side project to the thing I track with daily, and I have now tracked exclusively on it for the two weeks before the trip (leaving the weekend of 2026-10-24), with MyFitnessPal fully replaced. During those two weeks I was fixing bugs and improving features on the go, and leaned on the eval suites to make sure each change did not break the agent. The deadline is the narrative tension, not a speed brag: never frame it as 'built in two weeks' (the app work runs Aug to Oct). Then enumerate what replaced MyFitnessPal, grouped not as a wall of bullets: diary with day navigation; search that ranks the food you meant first, backed by USDA FoodData Central and Open Food Facts; barcode scan that falls back to asking for a label photo and saves it; photo of a plate or label sent to Gordon with Undo and Edit on what he logged; copy yesterday's meals; saved meals, recipes, favorites; goal wizard and adaptive calorie targets that learn from what you ate and what the scale did; 14 micronutrients; water and caffeine; weekly report; trends you can scrub, with where each macro came from; a pantry filled from a receipt and EAT NEXT suggestions; scheduled alerts where Gordon reaches out first; offline logging. The app section: React Native with Expo (SDK 57, expo-router), web app in Vite + React on Vercel, both sharing packages/app-core. Native features: Siri via a Swift App Intent ('Log food in Gordon'; friction: 'Tell Gordon' went to Contacts and 'Ask Gordon' made Siri ask 'Messages or Gordon?'), an Apple Watch app in SwiftUI with the calorie ring, macros and a talk page, hold-to-talk voice, push notifications for Gordon's replies, haptics, over-the-air updates for JS-only fixes. Friction worth including: TestFlight started refusing installs from build 4 on, so installs went back to local builds pushed to the phone with devicectl. It is the same Gordon agent on Telegram, web, phone and watch. Tease that the following parts cover the platform, memory, evals and the agent itself. Link back to Part 1. Close honestly: the trip is the test; an open question about whether I keep logging on a beach is fair game.

How a single-user Telegram bot was reorganized so a web app and a phone app could use the same agent and data. Moments: core/ extracted out of the MCP server with userId threaded through every function; a users table and row-level security; a forward-only SQL migration runner; a Hono REST API with JWT auth as a third Cloud Run service; a dev Supabase project evals cannot escape from; packages/app-core as the non-rendering layer both apps share (query wiring, units, dates, trends) with zero runtime dependencies, after a react-native-web shim was considered and rejected; 'generate, don't share or copy': the phone's design tokens are generated from the web app's CSS @theme, the API client is generated, and CI fails on drift; CI that blocks a deploy whose schema migration is not applied yet, and a credential scan added after .env.local leaked into a commit. Gordon's app turns run through the same queue and worker as Telegram, with the reply pushed. Include a Mermaid of the platform: Telegram and the apps -> ingest/API -> Cloud Tasks -> worker -> orchestrator/agents -> core -> Supabase. Link back to Part 1 and Part 2.

Memory, classified from the code. Long-term in Supabase: episodic (food_log, workout_log, water_log, body_metrics: what happened, queried by tools on demand, never auto-recalled), semantic (user_facts, upsert so the newest statement wins; nutrition_goals keep history with effective_from so switching cut to bulk does not re-grade past days), procedural (saved meals, recipes, favorites, pantry). Short-term: Agent SDK session transcripts on the container's disk, with only the session id in Supabase, 4-hour idle expiry; deferred_state for open questions; pending_routing. Not memory: chat_messages is the app's transcript and the model never reads it ('a record of what was said, not Gordon's memory'); caches (custom_foods, prompt cache, phone's offline copy). The counter-intuitive hook: on Cloud Run the session files live on ephemeral disk, so the 4-hour window is a polite fiction; a recycled instance loses the transcript, the SDK says 'No conversation found', the pointer is wiped and the facts in Supabase are what actually carry over. Other moments: 'answering Gordon's question no longer loses his tools' (resuming a deferred session dropped the MCP tools, so the fix passes the original message, question and answer as text into a fresh session); without today's date in the prompt Gordon invented dates; 'today' was Los Angeles time for everyone; 'last seven days' was eight; 30 copies of one protein powder in the cache because NULLs are distinct in a UNIQUE constraint; the CLI's auto-memory switched off on purpose (autoMemoryEnabled: false) because the agents keep memory in user_facts. VERIFY before writing: as of 2026-10-22 user facts were NOT injected at session start (prompts tell the model to call recall_user_facts) despite MEMORY.md saying otherwise; describe whatever the code does at write time. Include a Mermaid of the memory layers. Link to earlier parts.

The eval suites, now eight: routing, tool-selection, faithfulness, memory-recall, question-answer, cost-ceiling, vision, app-photo. Frame through the Part 2 period: two weeks of daily changes made on the go, with evals as the thing that said I had not broken the agent. Friction moments: tool-selection was not running each agent with production's query() options, so it tested a different agent than the one shipping; suites leaked state into each other until each one started clean; evals inherited the developer's CLAUDE.md until settingSources: [] was set; a vision suite added alongside the fix where label photos failed with a 400; a docs entry that retracted half the evidence on an open item. Verify in the repo how evals run in CI today (evals-pr.yml filters by changed area) and the thresholds, rather than repeating the June numbers. Link to earlier parts.

Commissioner Gordon as an agent: how the agent behind the app works. Part 2 already covers food search (the search_food contract, the four parallel sources, the 50% coverage floor and the 'nespresso double shot' burgers, the saved/frequency bonus) and the 'he picks the food, the data has the numbers' rule: link back to Part 2 for those and do NOT re-explain them. Cover instead: log_food's contract (food_id plus either grams or servings + unit; a servings log against a food with no gram weight returns needs: grams and Gordon asks, instead of inventing a conversion); one canonical food shape with an adapter per source (USDA, USDA branded, lab, Open Food Facts, custom, recipe) and the bugs that shaped it: branded foods logging zero calories, Open Food Facts vitamins C and D off by 1,000x and 1,000,000x, a measure confused with a number of servings, 'stop asking a model what arithmetic answers', working out what a cup weighs instead of refusing to log it; questions held open with AskUserQuestion instead of asked in prose (the dontAsk permission mode turned 'ask' into a deny, fixed with a PreToolUse defer hook), and answering a question dropping his tools on resume; set_goal_plan using the wizard's math; current-generation models per agent, all at low effort, and the bug where per-agent effort was silently ignored; the byte-stable daily prompt for prompt caching. Persona: warm but authoritative detective, addresses the user as Batman/Bruce; include one short real-feeling exchange. Mention Alfred and Ra's only briefly; Ra's gets his own post later. Include a Mermaid of Gordon's slice (orchestrator -> Gordon -> nutrition tools -> core -> providers + Supabase). Link to earlier parts.

NOT SCHEDULED: do not draft until the user moves this to planned. The Claude Code dev workflow: /bug files and triages a GitHub issue, /triage, /fix and fix-ready-bugs, /release (one OTA update or one build, plus a checklist) and /release verify; triage agent without Edit, fixer agent in its own worktree that never pushes to main or merges; phone feel bugs go to a human. Permission rules in .claude/settings.json reorganized to cut interruptions while anything that reaches production or users still asks. Re-verify the settings at write time.
